hyps.why: Stepping down from an already-large learning rate pulls training back from divergence, as in runs 10 and 17.
Raising an already-large learning rate pushes training into instability.
Very strong L2 penalty causes underfitting, as seen in runs 86 and 98.
Relaxing an excessive L2 penalty frees capacity, as in run 85.
Deeper nets with noisier small-batch gradients are more prone to instability, as in runs 22, 27 and 36.
Small batches give noisy gradients, so a higher learning rate more easily destabilizes training.
Increasing a very small batch reduces gradient noise, as in run 26.
Extra L2 regularization on deep networks tends to hurt, as in runs 82, 86, 87, 97 and 100.
Deep ReLU nets diverge more readily at high learning rates, as in run 16.
Small batches combined with a high learning rate amplify gradient noise and cause collapse, as in run 27.
